data.name: Version 9.0.0
data.body:
## What's Changed

This is a **major new release** with several important improvements:

- **C++17 is now required.**  
  Users who need to stay on C++11 or C++14 should continue using the 8.x series (we will continue to provide patches for it as needed).

- **No C++ standard library required at runtime (optional).**  
  Thanks to excellent work by [@mitchellh](https://github.com/mitchellh), you can now compile `simdutf` in a freestanding mode that does not depend on the C++ standard library. See the README for configuration details.

- **`fastbase64` command-line tool significantly upgraded.**  
  It is now a fast drop-in replacement for the standard `base64` utility. On large inputs, it can be several times faster than common alternatives.

- **New compile-time base64 literal.**  
  You can now conveniently declare base64-encoded arrays directly in code using the `_base64` suffix:  
  ```cpp
  auto data = "SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ="_base64;  // decoded at compile time into a byte array
  ```

- **Base64 API extended.**  
  We have added `base64_to_binary_details` to provide more detailed decoding information.


### Details

* Increase fuzzing test coverage by @anonrig in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/948
* fix some ppc64 problems by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/952
* Better fastbase64 + man pages by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/947
* allow end user to have base64 literals  by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/956
* extends our base64 public API by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/955
* reduce the size of our tools by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/958
* arm kernel should not define SIMDUTF_SIMD_HAS_BYTEMASK by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/960
* simpler approach to removing the C++ lib dependency at runtime by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/962


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/compare/v8.2.0...v9.0.0

data.name: Version 8.0.0
data.body:
## Major changes

The major change in this release is that now most simdutf functions are immediate functions (constexpr), i.e., they can be executed at compile time. Thus, for example, you can validate that a string is proper UTF-8 at compile time:

```
static_assert(simdutf::validate_utf8(s));
```

The constexpr interface requires C++23. (You can still use simdutf with C++11.)

Another major change is the introduction of a C API. You can now easily call simdutf from C (although you still need to link against a C++ library, either statically or at runtime). This C API should make it easier to write wrappers to simdutf from other programming languages. We now include a C header as part of our releases.

## What's Changed

* make most of simdutf constexpr by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/868
* add C API by @lemire https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/897
* fix bug in utf8_length_from_utf16() on big endian by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/884
* interop with std::text_encoding by @shikharish in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/881
* polish the functions in encoding_types.h by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/894
* ensure the override keyword is used everywhere by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/906
* Fix heap-buffer-overflow in convert_utf16_to_utf8_safe by @OwenSanzas in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/912
* fixing issue 914 (convert_latin1_to_utf8_safe is missing from the C api) by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/915
* Fix typos by @kianmeng in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/888
* Update/optimize Loongson kernels by @lemire https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/885

Because we fixed a couple of bugs, including a potential buffer overflow in `convert_utf16_to_utf8_safe `, we recommend that all users of the library update to 8.0.0. There are no breaking changes.

## What's Changed
* improving support for legacy GCC and validate_utf16_as_ascii by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/833 This fixes both https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/issues/832 and https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/issues/831

The new feature of this minor release is that we can check whether an UTF-16 string is 'ASCII' meaning that it can be converted to ASCII without any loss. This was requested by @trflynn89 of the [Ladybird](https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird) project.

```Cpp
/**
 * Validate the ASCII string as a UTF-16 sequence.
 * An UTF-16 sequence is considered an ASCII sequence
 * if it could be converted to an ASCII string losslessly.
 *
 * Overridden by each implementation.
 *
 * @param buf the UTF-16 string to validate.
 * @param len the length of the string in bytes.
 * @return true if and only if the string is valid ASCII.
 */
simdutf_warn_unused bool validate_utf16_as_ascii(const char16_t *buf,
                                                 size_t len) noexcept;
```

data.name: Version 7.3.4
data.body:
## What's Changed
* fixing Issue 824 by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/825 We are fixing a minor issued (defined as standard compliance with [TC39 base64 proposal](https://tc39.es/proposal-arraybuffer-base64/spec/#sec-frombase64)).  When using last_chunk_handling::stop_before_partial, we would sometimes we would either consume too many or too few characters, the difference being due to ignorable characters. Thus, for a string made entirely of spaces, we might report consuming no character whereas the proposed standard wants us to consume all characters. Conversely, when stopping before a partial chunk, we would consume all characters up to that point, whereas the proposed standard would want us to consume no trailing ignorable characters. Thanks to @syg for the report. Ping to @trflynn89, @Constellation, and @anonrig. We added corresponding tests.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/compare/v7.3.3...v7.3.4

data.name: Version 7.0.0
data.body:
## What's Changed

- We added a parameter, `decode_up_to_bad_char`, to the `base64_to_binary_safe` function. This parameter is disabled by default. When set to `true`, it addresses an issue in JavaScript engines (see [WebKit Bug 290829](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=290829)) where decoding should continue up to the point of an invalid character (including extra padding characters like `=`). This option is off by default due to a performance penalty when errors are encountered. **Maintainers of JavaScript engines relying on simdutf are urged to update.**
   ```C++
  auto r = simdutf::base64_to_binary_safe(
      input.data(), input.size(), outbuf.data(), outlen, options, last_chunk_options,
      decode_up_to_bad_char);
  ```
   C++20 users are reminded that the simdutf library supports spans, so ` input.data(), input.size()` can be replaced by `input`. And so forth.  E.g, the following syntax is possible:
   ```C++
  const auto [r, outlen] = simdutf:base64_to_binary_safe(
      input, outbuf, options, last_chunk_options, decode_up_to_bad_char);
  ```
- We introduced a new function, `atomic_base64_to_binary_safe`, to complement `atomic_binary_to_base64`. The usage of `simdutf:atomic_base64_to_binary_safe` is identical to `simdutf:base64_to_binary_safe`. Both `atomic_binary_to_base64` and `atomic_base64_to_binary_safe` are designed for scenarios where binary data is shared between threads, preventing undefined behavior. Specifically, `atomic_binary_to_base64` uses atomic *reads*, while `atomic_base64_to_binary_safe` uses atomic *writes*. Both atomic functions incur a performance cost, though this release optimizes the performance of `atomic_binary_to_base64`. These functions are not documented in our README.md, as they target specific use cases.
- We now hybrid base64 decoding. In this scenario, we can decode base64 content that uses both the default base64 and the base64 url alphabet. The Node.js engine implements base64 in this manner (although it is not documented). So instead of passing `simdutf::base64_options::base64_default`or `simdutf::base64_options::base64_url` as an option parameter to a base64 decoding function, you can pass `simdutf::base64_options::base64_default_or_url`. If you want to ignore garbage characters in the input, you can pass `simdutf::base64_options::base64_default_accept_garbage`, `simdutf::base64_options::base64_url_accept_garbage` or `simdutf::base64_options::base64_default_or_url_accept_garbage`.

We recommend that all users of our base64 encoder or decoder upgrade, as we have identified and fixed (non-critical) bugs. We have also improved the performance in many instances.

Credit: @pauldreik, @tantei3  and @WojciechMula made this release possible. 👏 👏 👏  Both @tantei3  and @WojciechMula have contributed major performance improvements. @pauldreik's work on the fuzzer is critical to quashing our bugs.

### Details

* recovering some of the lost speed in utf-32 to utf-16 (arm) when there is no surrogate handling by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/750
* arm64: alternate base64 decode logic to optimize base64url decode by @tantei3 in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/753
* Add the python script to generate the LUT used in NEON by @tantei3 in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/754
* Adding Relaxed write version for base64_to_binary_safe by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/752
* atomic_binary_to_base64 is too atomic: the requested feature was atomic reads by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/756
* RVV: faster valid UTF-32 to UTF-8 by @WojciechMula in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/759
* fix missing const in std::span inputs by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/764
* LoongArch64: implement `to_well_formed_utf16` by @WojciechMula in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/758
* Address WebKit Issue 290829: Maximize output in base64_to_binary_safe when an invalid character is encountered. by @lemire in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/762
* improve atomic_base64_to_binary_safe by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/766
* accelerate atomic base64 without simd by @pauldreik in https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf/pull/770
